sentences.text: This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 23.05.2020 at about 10.30 a.m., the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 23-E-1831 towards Billapura on Attibele-Sarjapura Road.

When he reached in front of A.K.Hollow Block Factor, Tyavakanahalli village, Bengaluru District, at that time the driver of Tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-D-5059 came from Bricks Factory in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's aforesaid motorcycle and caused the accident.
Consequent to which he fell down unconscious and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, he was shifted to Sri Sai Hospital, Yadavanahalli, Anekal Taluk, Bangalore wherein took treatment as an inpatient from 23.05.2020 to 03.06.2020 and again the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient at Ramaiah Medical college Hospital from 10.06.2020 to 11.06.2020 and thereafter the petitioner took treatment at Oxford Medical College Hospital and Research Centre as an inpatient from 15.06.2020 to 30.06.2020 and underwent surgery i.e., for proximal tibial open reduction internal fixation with plating lateral plating/GNS-5 hiled lat, plate on 17.06.2020.

REASONS 13.
Issue No.1:-

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 23.05.2020 at 10.30 a.m., when he was riding his motorcycle bearing No.KA-23-E- 1831 towards Billapura on Attibele -Sarjapura road, at that time the driver of Tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51- D-5059 came from Bricks Factory in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner vehicle and caused the accident.
P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.

14. In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle, PW.1 has relied upon the Ex.P1 to 10 which are the police records such as F.I.R., complaint, statement in crime No.80/2020, spot mahazar, seizure mahazar, notice issued u/sec.133 of IMV Act, reply to the above notice, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet etc.
15.
The respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.

It is vehemently submitted by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that there is inordinate delay of 10 days in lodging the complaint and that delayed complaint was lodged against unknown driver and police have falsely implicated the offending vehicle in the accident and filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle in collusion with the driver, owner and the petitioner.

The learned counsel by referring the case sheet has submitted that petitioner has given first hand information before the hospital authorities about the history of injury as "self fall from the two wheeler" hence,
same is recorded in the medical records, thereafter medical records were manipulated and cause of injury was changed from "self fall" to "hit by Tipper lorry" hence the learned counsel submitted to dismiss the petition.

16. The learned counsel at this juncture has referred the ruling reported in 2009 (15) SCC 165 and 2009 ACJ 293 and MFA 444/2016 wherein it was observed that "the absence of any complaint being lodged at an earliest point of time and the specific mention being made before the doctor regarding cause of injuries showing it is not due to involvement of offending vehicle makes the situation.

19. In MFA No.8124/2011 (MV)-Karnataka High Court _dated 07/11/2016- Para 6&7 -the settled position of law is that the Tribunal should not and ought not to place much reliance on the judgment of the Criminal court while considering the issue of factum of the accident and the consequent negligence of the driver of the vehicle.
It is incumbent on the tribunal to examine the evidence before it independently dehors any finding of the Criminal court on the question of the driver pleading guilty.
At the most, the circumstances of the driver pleading guilty may be considered as one of the piece of evidence to support of the case of the claimants.

It is further held in that Case that the said observation is made by the Court with the full knowledge that there has been spate of cases wherein false claims have been made before the Claims Tribunal and false implications are also on the increase.

This court, in several such cases, has found that a self- accident is given a turn and it is made to appear as an accident involving the motor cycle".
20.
In MFA No.201689/2016 (DB) DD 30/11/2020 Hon'ble High Court held that final report is not a conclusive proof in proceeding before the tribunal.

The Hon'ble court held that "Experience of the recent past shows instances of fraudulent/collusive involvement of motor vehicle duly covered by insurance policy in accident cases are burgeoning and if the insurance companies are saddled with the burden of challenging the charge sheets filed throughout the country without there being no clear mandate to do so, their work would be seriously crippled and they would not be able to do their insurance business without enhancing the premium, thereby further burdening the ever suffering owners of motor vehicles.
Even the most liberal reading the provisions of the motor vehicles act 1988 does not spell out such requirement".

21. In MFA No.962/2007 decided on 12.03.2009, whereby this court had made observations in much as false cases being filed before the Tribunal and also given direction to the Tribunals to put themselves on guard and to see that no person is allowed to abuse the process of law and make unlawful gain to himself by suppressing the true facts.

The Division Bench of the court in the case of VEERAPP, after analyzing the trend of the false claims going up has observed that the experience has shown that this branch of law is slowly getting in to the hands of unscrupulous people who are making mockery of the judicial process.

A disturbing trend of unholy alliance among the police, the doctors, the lawyers and sometimes even the insurance company, to siphon out the public money and to make an unlawful gain is fast emerging.
It is also gaining respectability and persons who indulge in such practices are acclaimed as most successful in their respective profession.
This is a dangerous trend, if unchecked would undermine the judicial process.
As the existing law in inadequate to check this malady, the courts not only have to be careful in adjudicating such claims but also find ways to prevent such abuse".

sentences.text: 29. In the background of the submissions made by the learned respective counsels, if the materials placed on record is perused, admittedly the accident in question has occurred on 23.05.2020 at 10.30 p.m., but the complaint came to be lodged on 02.06.2020 at 2.30 p.m.
There is delay nearly 10 days in lodging the complaint.
The complaint is lodged by the uncle of the petitioner who admittedly not an eye witness to the accident.

Though in the complaint it is stated that at the time of shifting the injured to the hospital he was unconscious but if the evidence of the petitioner who got examined as PW.1 is perused, the PW.1 in an unequivocal terms has deposed that on the date of accident itself his statement was recorded.
PW.1 is BBA graduate working in Silver Trust Clothing Pvt Ltd., situated in Gurgunte on contract basis.
It means petitioner is well educated person.

When petitioner himself has stated that he has given statement regarding the accident on the date of accident itself then it can be presumed that petitioner was in conscious state of mind at the time of his admission to the hospital.
Hence, it can also be presumed that, petitioner himself has given the history of injury before the treated doctor.
But for the reason best known to the petitioner, his statement given at an earliest point of time was not produced before the court and same has been suppressed.
30. The learned counsel for petitioner has referred about the police intimation allegedly sent from Sri Sai Hospital which is at Ex.P24.

The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the genuineness of Ex.P24 stating that there is no endorsement in the Ex.P24 about receipt of the intimation by the jurisdictional police.

Keeping the objection raised regarding the genuineness of the Ex.P24 intact, if for the sake of discussion it is accepted as true that intimation was sent as per Ex.P24 to the jurisdictional PS from Sri Sai Hospital intimation then in order to send such police intimation, the case has to be registered as Medico Legal case.
Though respondent no.2 has disputed the whole medical records but the petitioner has not summoned or produced the MLC register maintained in Sri Sai Hospital.
When serious dispute was raised regarding the history of injuries sustained due to RTA "Hit by lorry," under such circumstances, the petitioner ought to have produce the MLC register.
If MLC register was produced it would have given clear picture about the history of injuries and it would have thrown much light on the case of the petitioner.

31. Even though the case was remanded to this court at the instance of the petitioner on the ground that he will adduce further evidence and will wxamine the author of Ex.P11 i.e., Discharge summary issued from Sri Sai Hospital, and even though this court had dismissed the claim petition interalia on the ground that the petitioner has not produced the MLC register maintained in Sri Sai hospital,
but even after remand, the petitioner has not thought it necessary to produce the MLC register recorded in Sri Sai hospital.
Having summoned the MRO of sri Sai hospital, for the reason best known to the petitioner he has not pressed the evidence of MRO.

As observed supra when there is serious inconsistency in the medical records regarding the cause of injuries sustained by the petitioner, under such circumstances the petitioner could have produced the MLC register even after the remand of the case.
32. Further if the medical records produced by the petitioner are perused, the discharge summary issued from Sri Sai Hospital is marked as Ex.P11/Ex.P30.

In the Ex.P11/Ex.P30 it is mentioned that B.N. Keerthiraj vs A.K. Concrete Blocks on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46400406/

Hence, in all the medical records maintained at an earliest point of time, the history of injury is shown as" skid and fall."

Though, the petitioner has relied upon Ex.P24 i.e., police intimation sent from Sri Sai Hospital, wherein history of injury is shown as RTA by driving two wheeler hit by lorry but as rightly stated by the counsel for the respondent no.2 there is no endorsement regarding the receipt of said police intimation by the jurisdictional police.
The name of police station date, time and seal of the said station is not affixed in the Ex.P24.
Further Ex.P24 is the carbon copy of police intimation.

Under such circumstances if really police intimation as per Ex.P24 was sent at an earliest of point of time definitely there would have been endorsement regarding receipt of police intimation by the jurisdictional police and in such an event, the police personals definitely would have attended the injured in the hospital to record his statement.
Though the petitioner has stated that on the date of accident itself his statement was recorded but the said statement allegedly given by the petitioner is not produced before the court.

33. Further there is ambiguity in the medical records regarding history of injury as in some documents issued from Sri Sai Hospital there is mention about involvement of two vehicles and in some medical records it is mentioned as self fall from the two wheeler.

It is true that, after the remand of the case, petitioner has examined Dr.Dhananjay Reddy - Consultant General / Gastro Surgeon at Sri Sai Hospital, Yadavanahalli as PW.5, the hospital at which petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 23-5-2020 to 03-06-2020.

PW.5 has deposed only about the treatment taken by the petitioner in their hospital as an inpatient on the H/o R.T.A from 23-05-2020 till 03-06-2020 and he has not stated anything about the MLC registered in their hospital.
If really the accident was due to the hit by offending vehicle, definitely MLC was registered in their hospital.

Even though this court while dismissing the claim petition had observed that the petitioner by not examining the Medical Officer of Sri Sai hospital have not clarified the inconsistency in the Medical records to say on what basis the said hospital have changed the history of injury from "self fall" to "hit by lorry", but the petitioner having summoned the PW.5 and having examined the PW.5, not elicited anything from his mouth regarding the examined H/o injury.

The PW.5 in his cross examination has admitted that, whenever patient is discharged from the hospital the copy of the discharge summary will be given to the patient and in the discharge summary it will be mentioned, to whom the copy of discharge summary is handed over.

It is further admitted by PW.5 that in the discharge summary which is in the case file, the Resident Medical officer has signed the discharge summary and in the said document the person to whom the copy of the discharge summary is issued is also mentioned.

sentences.text: By examining the PW.5 the petitioner has not clarified the ambiguity in the Ex.P11/Ex.P30 (discharge summary issued from Sri Sai hospital) and the discharge summary issued from the very same hospital, which is in the case sheet.
As observed supra, in the Ex.P11 and P30 the H/o injury is mentioned as " riding two wheeler, hit by lorry.

" 
Whereas, in the discharge summary which is in the case sheet H/o injury is mentioned as "self fall from the two wheeler."
34. Further the petitioner even has not examined the investigation officer and the eye witness to the accident to speak about the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Further petitioner for the reason best known to him has not produced MLC register maintained by Sri Sai Hospital.
35. It is further relevant to observe here that as per the case of petitioner the driver of the offending vehicle by driving it in rash and negligent manner hit against the vehicle of the petitioner.
If that being the case definitely some amount of damage would have been caused to the offending vehicle.
But if Ex.P8 is perused no damage was caused to the offending vehicle even any scratch mark.
The said fact would also creates doubt in the mind of the court about the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
36. Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the judgment rendered by Hon'ble High court in MFA No 2006/2010 C/w MFA No 1763/2010 dated 20/7/2018:

In the said case the earliest medical record placed on record show that the claimant had sustained injuries because of fall from his own motorcycle near the parked lorry, the FIR was lodged one month after the alleged incident with no plausible explanation for the delay brooked in such lodging, even ExP3 which is mahazar also does not mention as to how the accident occurred except stating that the lorry is involved and strangely registration number was not mentioned.

In the given set of facts it was held that earliest version of the claimant as found from the medical records should be taken as in the medical records it was shown that the petitioner sustained injury due to self fall, further delay of one month in lodging the complaint which create doubt in the mind of the court about the genuineness of the case of the petitioner.
Hence Hon'ble High court has dismissed the claim petition.

37. In MFA No 6682/2015 dated 16/12/2022: In the said case also there was delay in lodging the complaint and MLC register discloses that the petitioner was riding a bike, skid and fall but the same has been altered as hit by bike

The Rw1 who is the medical officer has also admitted in his evidence that they have made alteration and history was given as he was riding a bike and fell down and same has been altered and no substantive piece of evidence placed before the court that some other person has given the history and it was admitted by Rw1 that injured was conscious at the time of his admitting to the hospital.

In the given set of facts it was observed by the hon'ble High court that firstly the history was given that petitioner fell down from bike while riding the motor cycle but the facts are twisted that he was walking along with two others and that because it is a case of self fall no intimation was sent to the jurisdictional police, hence the petitioner cooked up the story of RTA hence claim petition was dismissed.

sentences.text: Now keeping in mind the observation made in the aforesaid judgment along with line of argument canvassed by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2, if the police records are perused, as observed supra there is delay of ten days in lodging the complaint without there being satisfactory explanation for delay except stating that petitioner was taking treatment.
If really police intimation as per Ex.P24 was sent from the hospital authority the police personnel's definitely would have recorded the statement of the petitioner in the hospital itself.
It is deposed by Pw-1 that he has stated the true facts before the police personal but, his statement is not available on record.

Hence the very documents placed on record and the very evidence of Pw-1 admitting certain material facts which creates doubt in the mind of the court about the genuineness of the case put forward by the petitioner and about the involvement of offending vehicle in the alleged accident.
It appears that the vehicle of the respondent No.1 is fixed later on to claim compensation in collusion with the respondent no 1, hence only respondent no 1 has remained exparte.
Hence considering the aforesaid material facts without going further to discuss about the rash and negligent aspect, this court answers issue no 1 in the Negative.
39. Issue No.2:- As this court has answered issue no 1 in the negative, the question of discussing issue No.2 does not arise.
Hence issue No.2 is also answered in the Negative.
40. Issue No.3: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is dismissed.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
Consequent to which he fell down unconscious and sustained grievous injuries.
Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy,
he was doing coolie work and thereby was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to do the said work.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
It is contended by the respondent no.2 that the FIR was lodged after 10 days of alleged accident against unknown driver of tipper lorry, later the jurisdictional police have falsely implicated the tipper lorry and that the alleged offending vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and that the driver of the offending lorry was not holding valid and effective driving licence B.N. Keerthiraj vs A.K. Concrete Blocks on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46400406/
2 and the said vehicle was not having valid permit to ply in place of accident.
Accordingly, the Hon'ble High Court was pleased to remand the matter with specific direction to the tribunal to grant reasonable opportunity to both sides for adducing evidence and for arguments and to dispose off the matter on merit by duly considering the entire evidence on record and to dispose off the case within two months from the date of order.
The respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 23.05.2020 at about 10.30 a.m., in front of A.K.Hollow Block Factory, Attibele Sarjapura road, Tyavakanahalli village, Bengaluru and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-D-5059 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is vehemently submitted by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that there is inordinate delay of 10 days in lodging the complaint and that delayed complaint was lodged against unknown driver and police have falsely implicated the offending vehicle in the accident and filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle in collusion with the driver, owner and the petitioner.
The learned counsel by referring the case sheet has submitted that petitioner has given first hand information before the hospital authorities about the history of injury as "self fall from the two wheeler" hence,
same is recorded in the medical records, thereafter medical records were manipulated and cause of injury was changed from "self fall" to "hit by Tipper lorry" hence the learned counsel submitted to dismiss the petition.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The alleged offending vehicle was not seized under the mahazar and no damage was caused to the alleged offending vehicle.
The complaint is lodged by the uncle of the petitioner who admittedly not an eye witness to the accident.
It means petitioner is well educated person.
When petitioner himself has stated that he has given statement regarding the accident on the date of accident itself then it can be presumed that petitioner was in conscious state of mind at the time of his admission to the hospital.
Hence, it can also be presumed that, petitioner himself has given the history of injury before the treated doctor.
But for the reason best known to the petitioner, his statement given at an earliest point of time was not produced before the court and same has been suppressed.
Keeping the objection raised regarding the genuineness of the Ex.P24 intact, if for the sake of discussion it is accepted as true that intimation was sent as per Ex.P24 to the jurisdictional PS from Sri Sai Hospital intimation then in order to send such police intimation, the case has to be registered as Medico Legal case.
When serious dispute was raised regarding the history of injuries sustained due to RTA "Hit by lorry," under such circumstances, the petitioner ought to have produce the MLC register.
If MLC register was produced it would have given clear picture about the history of injuries and it would have thrown much light on the case of the petitioner.
PW.5 pleaded ignorance whether the treatment taken by the petitioner is registered in the MLC or not.
If that being the case definitely some amount of damage would have been caused to the offending vehicle.
The said fact would also creates doubt in the mind of the court about the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Hence Hon'ble High court has dismissed the claim petition.
